studies.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls — Gematria Discernment Companion
studies.summary: A modern computational and contemplative companion using standard Hebrew gematria for declared Hebrew spellings and four transparent modern English ciphers, with numerical equality treated as a prompt for comparison rather than evidence of historical or supernatural identity.

computationalMethod.name: Hebrew gematria plus four modern English comparison ciphers
computationalMethod.method: Hebrew values use the declared Hebrew spelling with standard letter values and standard values for final forms. English comparisons report English Ordinal, Full Reduction, Reverse Ordinal, and Reverse Reduction; spaces, punctuation, accents, and hyphens are ignored. Digital roots are modern contemplative reductions produced by repeated decimal digit summation.
computationalMethod.reproducibilityNote: Report the spelling and all four English totals rather than selecting only favorable matches. The companion grades exact four-cipher matches above exact single-cipher matches above shared root patterns; none establishes historical or supernatural identity.

studies.title: The Qur'an in Abjad — Number, Structure, and Discernment
studies.summary: A transparent computational study of the 6,236-verse Arabic source corpus using Eastern Abjad values, declared normalization and sensitivity rules, verse/surah/title/vocabulary totals, and explicit interpretive restraint. Arithmetic patterns are not independent proof of doctrine, prophecy, divine intention, miracle, or hidden code.

normalizationProfile.name: Qur'an in Abjad — primary Arabic normalization
rules: Remove harakat and recitation marks; they are not independent Abjad letters.
Unify graphic alif forms أ إ آ ٱ to ا with value 1.
Treat alif maqsura ى as ي with value 10 in the primary method.
For hamza carriers ؤ and ئ, count the carrier letter و or ي.
Treat ta marbuta ة as ه with value 5 in the primary method; sensitivity analysis also tests ت = 400.
Treat standalone hamza ء as 0 in the primary method; sensitivity analysis tests hamza as alif = 1.
Spaces and punctuation contribute 0; only Arabic letters contribute.
normalizationProfile.sourcePolicy: The source edition remains unchanged apart from trimming outer whitespace. Analytical normalization is applied only inside the Abjad study.

computationalMethod.name: Eastern Abjad additive analysis
computationalMethod.method: Assign Eastern Abjad values from 1 through 1000 to normalized Arabic letters and add letter values for phrases, verses, surahs, titles, and vocabulary; also report token and normalized-letter counts, exact repeated verse strings, and modern digital-root reductions where used.
computationalMethod.reproducibilityNote: Results are corpus- and normalization-dependent. Keep the source hashes and normalization profile visible; arithmetic identity proves arithmetic identity, while theological conclusions require independent historical, linguistic, and interpretive support.
